title: Thermal-shutdown trip/reset temperature and hysteresis (auto-restart)
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Thermal" row (Tj <= 125C operating ceiling; theta_JA delegated to package/integration) via spec/decision-records/DR-005-thermal-shutdown-trip.md's ratified thermal-shutdown target (Tj_trip = 150C nominal untrimmed, hysteresis 15C nominal / Tj_reset ~135C, auto-restart/non-latching) against the CTAT-sense + comparator + hysteresis circuit #29 added to design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch. DR-005 is ratified by issue #1 / DR-006 -- the bounds below cite it verbatim, not an invented final number. Method: a continuous ngspice DC '.dc temp' sweep, ascending then descending in one session (DC continuation captures the comparator's hysteresis the same way a Schmitt-trigger characterization does), watching V(VOUT) collapse (trip, M_TSHUT engages and turns M_PASS off) and recover (reset, auto-restart) -- see the testbench schematic's header for the full derivation. 125C-vs-150C corner-coverage decision (required before this testbench could even be written, per this issue's own acceptance criteria): DR-004 pins this repo's PVT-corner verification temperature axis at {-40, 27, 125}C, but DR-005's 150C nominal trip sits above that pin. This testbench extends temperature coverage past 125C specifically for this one thermal-shutdown testbench (option (a) of DR-005's Consequences section, formalized in this issue's addendum to DR-005 and design/README.md's Known-gaps section, both dated 2026-08-25) rather than accepting the gap (option (b)) -- chosen because an empirical check (ngspice + the pinned sky130 BSIM models on a diode-connected core device, 2026-08-25) confirmed the models solve without numerical failure (no NaN/divergence/error) continuously from -40C to 200C, so extending is mechanically possible; the tradeoff accepted explicitly is that points above 125C are running those models in extrapolation beyond DR-004's characterized range, not confirmed against silicon, so the measured trip/reset numbers carry lower confidence than a PVT-corner point inside the pinned axis. This does not change DR-004's binding for the other four testbenches (load-transient/psrr-dc/dropout-vs-load/loop-gain) or for spec verification generally -- it is a scoped extension for this testbench only. INITIAL-CONDITION CONTRACT (#171, seeded by #178): both '.dc temp' sweeps used to release from ngspice's own unconstrained Newton solve with EN already at a constant enabled level -- the defect class #164/#171 characterize -- and the superseded record 20260825-104426-933dfdd carries a solver diagnostic on 14 of its 15 corner logs, which sim/bin/corner-run.py's #171 gate now forces to FAIL outright. The testbench now carries a '.nodeset' card seeding the ascending sweep's own starting point (TEMP = 80C, block regulating and untripped) with the node set of a settled cold-start 'uic' transient of this same testbench at tt/80C/vsup=3.30V (V(VOUT) 1.80076, FB 1.20070, N_FBB 0.600445, EA_OUT = EA_CZ 2.48682, SS 3.29980, BIASP 2.32652, NB 0.803915, EA_TAIL 2.46374, TS_CMP 3.29974, TS_SNS 1.46284, TS_REF 1.13593, AMP_ENN 0.00253779 V, settled 2.5ms-3ms tail, zero solver diagnostics) -- i.e. a measured physically realizable state of this circuit, not a guess. WHY '.nodeset' RATHER THAN THE CONTRACT'S TWO NAMED SHAPES, measured not assumed: a temperature sweep cannot be a transient (ngspice has no time-varying TEMP), so the 'uic' + EN-edge shape #170/#172/#178 used for mc-output-accuracy, line-/load-regulation and dropout-vs-load is unavailable here; and '.ic' does not reach a 'dc' analysis at all -- ngspice applies it to the operating-point solve preceding a non-'uic' transient, which #178 measured directly on the sibling dropout-vs-load bench (tt/125C/3.30V: an eleven-node '.ic' copied verbatim from sim/ic-screen-125c-b leaves the flail intact, singular matrix x6, dynamic gmin stepping failed x16, out of range for ^ x13). '.nodeset' is the weaker mechanism (a first-iteration constraint that is then released rather than a held state), so the evidence that this bench now conforms is the measured absence of solver diagnostics in the record, not the mechanism's pedigree. ONE SEED VALUE CORRECTED BY #189, which is what closed the gate: #178's record 20260926-052517-eba96ae did NOT reach zero diagnostics -- it fell from 14 of 15 corner logs to 2 of 15, with 'ss_27c_2.97v' and 'sf_27c_2.97v' still tripping the #171 gate on 'Dynamic gmin stepping failed'. #189 located those failures (at TEMP = 144/146/148C at 'ss_27c_2.97v', the three points immediately below the 150.658C crossing the run then reported) and traced them to a single misclassified value in the card: EA_TAIL was written VIN-relative ('{vsup-0.836}') although it is the SOURCE node of the error amplifier's PMOS input pair, i.e. one |Vgs| above the pair's ground-referenced gate voltages rather than one drop below VIN. Three clean cold-start 'uic' settles at ss/80C, one per supply on the corner axis, measure EA_TAIL's supply slope at 0.24 V/V (2.42179 / 2.50138 / 2.57694 V at 2.97 / 3.30 / 3.63V) against 0.97-1.02 V/V for the genuinely VIN-tracking nodes (EA_OUT, SS, BIASP, TS_CMP), so the VIN-relative form put the seed 288mV below the real node at 2.97V. The card now carries EA_TAIL as the absolute 2.4637 V -- the SAME number #178 measured at tt/80C/3.30V, with only its supply classification fixed; no new value is invented and no per-supply seed mechanism is needed, because the residual was never a per-supply-derivation gap. A related measurement worth recording: the card is re-applied as the first-iteration guess at EVERY 'dc temp' point, not only the sweep's first -- correcting one value took the ascending sweep at 'ss_27c_2.97v' from needing gmin stepping at essentially all 51 points to needing it at 3, which a first-point-only seed could not do. TWO LIMITS STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: (1) '.nodeset' is a netlist card, so both 'dc temp' commands share it -- it is the right state at the ascending sweep's 80C start and a deliberately wrong (but harmless, first-guess-only) one at the descending sweep's 180C start, where the block is expected to be tripped; ngspice offers no per-analysis nodeset. (2) This bench's trip == reset degeneracy (hysteresis_c == 0 at most corners) is NOT the seeding question -- it is the pre-existing DC-continuation limitation #77 found and #91 carries forward, and neither #178 nor #189 fixes or worsens it. What a conforming measurement of a hysteretic trip point would have to be, if that degeneracy is ever to be closed, is stated in sim/README.md's '#189' section: a temperature staircase of independent cold-start 'uic' transients (one per TEMP point, each starting from EN = 0 with C_OUT discharged) for the trip direction, and the same staircase released from a tripped-state seed for the reset direction -- two decks, not one 'dc temp' continuation. #189 did not attempt it; it is not needed for the trip point this bench bounds, and ngspice's lack of a time-varying TEMP is what forces it to be a staircase of separate runs rather than one analysis.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: * temperature_c above (27) is a placeholder only -- this experiment sweeps
* TEMP itself as the analysis variable (see claim); the corner matrix's real
* axes here are process and supply_v, not temperature. 2C step (rather than
* a finer one) is a deliberate runtime/resolution tradeoff: DR-005's own
* trip/hysteresis targets are untrimmed and PVT-loose (15C nominal hysteresis
* window), so resolving the crossing to +/-2C costs negligible accuracy
* against that window while keeping each corner's continuation sweep
* (~100 points ascending + descending, each needing gmin-stepped
* convergence) tractable.
* Floor of 80C (not the 100C DR-004 top-of-range would suggest) is
* deliberate: the fast-PMOS-skew corners (sf especially) trip as low as
* ~101C (empirically confirmed, 2026-08-25, issue #66), and ngspice's own
* '.meas dc ... find/when ... fall=1' has a confirmed edge-of-sweep
* artifact -- if the crossing falls within the FIRST swept interval
* (i.e. no data point precedes it), the interpolated result is garbage
* (observed: 1.15e7 instead of ~101 for sf/3.30V when the sweep started
* at exactly 100C). Starting well below the coldest observed trip point
* keeps every real crossing away from that edge case. This is an ngspice
* measurement-technique limitation, not a circuit finding -- noted here
* so a future re-run does not reintroduce it by narrowing the range.
* Each '.dc temp' analysis opens its own ngspice plot (dc1, dc2); a bare
* vector reference after the second analysis starts resolves against the
* CURRENT (dc2) plot, so trip_temp_c (a dc1 result) needs an explicit
* dc1. prefix once dc2 is active -- reset_temp_c/hysteresis_c need no
* prefix since they are computed while dc2 is still current.
* Both sweeps below are seeded by the testbench's own IC_SEED `.nodeset`
* card at the ASCENDING sweep's 80C starting point (issue #178, the #171
* initial-condition contract). A temperature sweep cannot be a `uic`
* transient, and ngspice does not apply `.ic` to a `dc` solve, so
* `.nodeset` is the only seed mechanism available here -- see the claim
* and the testbench header for the measurement behind both statements.
* One value in that card (EA_TAIL) was corrected by #189 from a
* `vsup`-relative to an absolute form, which is what took the last two
* corners (`ss_27c_2.97v`, `sf_27c_2.97v`) off the #171 gate; the card is
* re-applied at EVERY point of both sweeps, not only the first, so a
* misclassified value biases the whole continuation rather than one point.
dc temp 80 180 2
meas dc trip_temp_c when v(vout)=0.9 fall=1
dc temp 180 80 -2
meas dc reset_temp_c when v(vout)=0.9 rise=1
let hysteresis_c = dc1.trip_temp_c - reset_temp_c

measurements.name: trip_temp_c
measurements.note: Rising-temperature trip point: the TEMP value where V(VOUT) first falls through 0.9V (roughly half the light-load regulated value) on the ascending 80-180C sweep (2C resolution). Bound: min=125C -- the spec's own Tj<=125C rated-operation ceiling (spec/target-spec.md's Thermal row); DR-005's Decision explicitly requires the trip to sit above rated operation, so a corner tripping at or below 125C is a genuine functional defect (see design/README.md's dated '45-point PVT + Monte Carlo campaign' section and issue #69), not a passing result under a looser reading. DR-005's own nominal target is 150C, but no upper bound is enforced here -- the reference is untrimmed/bias-generator-derived and explicitly PVT-loose (DR-005 Consequences), so this measurement reports the actual number rather than gating on the nominal target.

measurements.name: reset_temp_c
measurements.note: Falling-temperature reset point: the TEMP value where V(VOUT) recovers back through 0.9V on the descending 180-80C sweep, i.e. auto-restart engaging. DR-005 target: Tj_reset ~135C nominal. No bound enforced here (untrimmed/PVT-loose per DR-005); reported for the record narrative and the hysteresis_c derivation below.

measurements.name: hysteresis_c
measurements.note: trip_temp_c - reset_temp_c. DR-005 target: 15C nominal. Bound: min=0 -- a genuine auto-restart hysteresis window must have reset_temp_c < trip_temp_c (positive feedback around the comparator per design/README.md's 'Thermal shutdown (#29)' section, item 5); a non-positive value would mean the hysteresis mechanism is not actually working, not just off-target. Resolution caveat: the 2C sweep grid means a measured value within +/-2C of zero should be read as 'no resolvable hysteresis at this grid step', not necessarily a confidently-signed defect -- see the record narrative for the per-corner reading. Methodology caveat (issue #77, 2026-08-25): this measurement's own default '.dc temp' continuation (plus ngspice's dynamic gmin-stepping convergence fallback) has been shown, at some corners, to lose track of a real hysteretic branch a nodeset-forced independent .op can still find -- and at other, more marginal corners, to land on essentially whichever branch the solver's exact numerical path happens to reach across a many-degree-wide flickering band with no single well-defined crossing. A single number here should therefore be read alongside design/README.md's dated '#77' section (under 'Thermal shutdown (#29)') and DR-005's second 2026-08-25 addendum before being treated as a confident per-corner measurement, not just this note's pre-existing +/-2C grid caveat. Not fixed by #77; carried forward by #91.
